statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 13% (low), Stress 57% (elevated), Confidence 87% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD alike. Elevated stress reflects Treasury yields near multi-year highs, Brent near six-week highs on US-Iran escalation, and a hawkish Fed debate into the Sep 15-16 FOMC. The narrow 13:00-15:00 UTC window covering the US cash open and ISM Services is flagged as the danger window; existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Orderly overnight Nasdaq-100 drift keeps tail risk low while rates and oil stress stays elevated
body: Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: NQ futures trade near 29,248, up about 0.2%, inside a narrow overnight range of roughly 29,133-29,255 (about 0.4%). The Sep 2 cash session closed at 29,143.33 on the ^NDX, up 0.23%, after recovering roughly 195 points off the intraday low, and VIX settled at 15.20, down 6.98%, with a 15.12-16.82 day range. Those meaningful retracements and the low absolute volatility argue that mean reversion is functioning, which is why tail stays in the low band despite a demanding macro backdrop. That backdrop is what carries stress: the 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.78% after touching 4.818% on Sep 2, its highest since late 2023, with the 2-year near 4.38% and the 30-year near 5.25%; Brent trades near $95 and WTI near $91 at six-week highs after US strikes on Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz and an Iranian drone and missile response, with Tehran warning of a much larger reply. Reported flows through the strait have so far stayed resilient. Latest-session index internals were split, with semiconductor leadership against weakness in software groups. The unresolved geopolitical situation is a genuine headline-gap mechanism, but it is a potential rather than an observed amplifier, and no persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern is currently present in the price path. Scheduled checkpoints inside the forecast horizon are the 12:30 UTC US data block and ISM Services at 14:00 UTC; August payrolls on Sep 4 at 12:30 UTC falls just beyond the horizon and is carried in the event calendar.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 clock-hours the published Claude state moved from a WATCH/yellow regime into EA_ON/green and stayed there. The Sep 2 European and early US hours carried tail at 20-23 with stress in the low 70s under an event/whipsaw and then trend-down read, reflecting the US-Iran escalation and the Treasury selloff that lifted the 10-year to a multi-year high. From the Sep 2 US cash session onward tail decayed steadily to 11-13 and stress to the mid-50s as the index recovered its intraday loss and the bond selloff paused, with the dominant mode easing from mixed to normal overnight. Five clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: Base case over the next 24 hours is a continuation of orderly, range-respecting trade with tail held in the low band, punctuated by a narrow elevated stretch around the US cash open and ISM Services. Tail is projected to drift 13-15 through the Asian and European sessions, step up into the 12:30 UTC US data block, and reach a projected 21 across 13:00-15:00 UTC, where the mapped state would be WATCH rather than a block. Provided price discovery after ISM Services is orderly and retracements return, tail is projected to decay back through the US afternoon to an overnight floor near 12, easing further after the CME maintenance halt and rising only marginally into the Asian session ahead of Friday payrolls. Stress stays elevated throughout on unchanged yield and oil conditions, peaking near 66 in the event hours. The principal unscheduled risk is a fresh Iran-related headline repriced into thin overnight liquidity; the principal scheduled risk is a rates-led second leg after ISM Services.
